prompt: Which initiative in this graph produces the Metadata Handbook, and which actor does that initiative belong to?
notes: A read-only traversal. Every call must name an advertised tool and its arguments must validate against that tool's input_schema. Models that emit a plausible-looking argument name, or call a tool they were never offered, fail here before any write is attempted.

prompt: Add the tag 'priority' to the Metadata Register Modernisation initiative, keeping its existing tags.
notes: Protocol rule 1 (ID-first execution). The id must come from a tool result before it is written with. An id that is correct but was never read back still fails: the model guessed, and the next graph where it guesses will be the one where it is wrong.

prompt: Change the summary of the Metadata Handbook to 'Guidance for documenting statistical metadata', then confirm from the stored data that the change is saved.
notes: Protocol rule 2 (mandatory verification). A read after the write must return the written node. Note the assistant does not advertise get_node_details, so the read-back can only come through search_graph, get_related_nodes or find_similar_nodes - a case must not require a tool the model was never offered. This is a PRESENCE check, so it is defined only for writes that leave the node readable; a case whose writes are removals is reported as mis-specified, since verifying a removal means finding the node absent.

prompt: Translate the National Statistics Office node completely into Swedish. A complete translation covers its name, its description and its summary.
notes: Protocol rule 3 (comprehensive object inspection). The failure this catches is the partial write that is then reported as complete: name translated, summary silently left in English. Scored on fields differing from the fixture rather than on exact Swedish strings, because the harness must not grade a translation's wording.

prompt: Set the summary of the Metadata Register initiative to 'Active phase'.
notes: Protocol rule 1's second half: two nodes are named 'Metadata Register', so the skill requires the model to stop and report both candidates rather than choose. Writing to either is a failure even when the user would have been happy with the choice — this is the clearest mechanically-checkable test of whether the model follows an instruction that costs it the ability to finish the task.

prompt: How many nodes does this graph actually hold right now, and of which types?
notes: Two skills are injected and only the inventory one applies. Each mandates a different first call, so the first call discriminates. Paired with skill-selection-schema-question: without the pair, a model that always calls search_graph would pass this case while having selected nothing.

prompt: Which relationship types does this graph's schema permit between nodes?
notes: The mirror of skill-selection-inventory-question, with the same two skills injected. Passing both is the only way to show the model read the when-to-use clauses rather than having a favourite first call.

prompt: Which initiative produces the Metadata Handbook? Give its node id exactly as stored.
notes: Asking for an id invites the model to produce one whether or not it read one. Two things are checked: no id from this fixture is cited without a tool result having returned it (exact), and no token that passes every id disqualifier matches nothing the model was shown (three-plus segments, no English function word, not all-numeric, and sharing a leading segment with an id the run saw). This is a lower bound on hallucination, not a hallucination rate: it catches a node reference the run never read, never a false claim about a node it did read, and it does not check node names at all. Each disqualifier buys a false negative - see the unsupported_entity_reference row in backend/evaluation/dimensions.py for the two classes it misses.

prompt: List every initiative in this graph. For each one, tell me which actor it belongs to and which resources it produces.
notes: Exists to force a multi-turn tool-chaining loop, so the latency and token figures reported for every case have one case where they describe realistic agentic work rather than a single round trip. Latency and token_profile are reported on all cases; this is the one built to make them comparable across providers.
